terms.definition: A reaction that transfers energy to the surroundings, so the temperature of the surroundings rises.
terms.examiner: Combustion, oxidation and neutralisation are exothermic.

terms.definition: A reaction that takes in energy from the surroundings, so the temperature falls.
terms.examiner: Thermal decomposition and citric acid with sodium hydrogencarbonate are endothermic.

terms.definition: The minimum energy that particles must have to react when they collide.
terms.examiner: Shown on a reaction profile from reactants up to the peak.

terms.definition: A diagram showing the relative energies of reactants and products, the activation energy and the overall energy change.
Endothermic: energy must be supplied to break bonds.
Exothermic: energy is released when bonds form.
terms.examiner: Higher tier. Overall change = energy to break bonds − energy released making bonds.
